Sony Life Insurance has suffered a cyberattack that exposed personal information from around 385,000 customers.  The unauthorized access was discovered on October 27, and Sony Life blocked external access to the affected systems from the morning of October 28.  The leaked information reportedly includes:  -Names -Dates of birth -Gender -Addresses -Phone numbers -Insurance policy numbers -Contract details  Sony Life says the leaked data does not include My Number information, credit card details, or bank account information used for insurance payments.

IoT機器などに組み込まれる軽量Webサーバー「GoAhead」で、TLS処理に関する脆弱性3件が明らかになった。FoxIOによると、設定次第で失効済みクライアント証明書の受け入れ、通信の復号、証明書チェーン長の制限回避が可能になる。影響は使用するTLSライブラリによって異なる。  最も深刻なCVE-2026-115881は、OpenSSL系を使い、相互TLSと証明書失効リストを設定したGoAhead 3.4.5～6.1.0に影響。失効リストを読み込んでも検証に使わず、無効化した証明書を受け入れてしまう。 Mbed TLSを使う4.0.2～6.1.0では、一部のTLS 1.2通信の暗号化が弱まり、条件を満たす通信記録を後から復号できる。LibreSSLの特定版を使う6.1.0以前には、証明書チェーン長の制限を回避できるCVE-2026-115884もある。 GoAhead 6.1.1はOpenSSLとMbed TLSの問題を修正。LibreSSLの問題には発行者検証の有効化やライブラリ変更が推奨される。FoxIOはPoCと検出用情報を公開したが、製品への修正配信は各メーカーに委ねられる。 securityweek.com/tls-flaws-f…

Aokigahara infostealer adds purpose-built collection routines targeting local AI coding assistants, marking a commodity malware shift that turns developer workstations into cloud and pipeline pivot points.  Key findings:  - Aokigahara (also tracked as Aoki, with possible lineage to Kamidere or Stygian) is a modular Windows infostealer first documented in 2026. Newer samples confirmed by independent analysis to have added AI-specific collection that earlier versions lacked, making this a family-level capability expansion, not just a configuration tweak. No operator or intrusion set attribution has been established.  - The dedicated routines harvest authentication files, session tokens, and local application databases from a broad product list: Claude Code and Desktop, ChatGPT Desktop, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, GitHub Copilot, Gemini CLI, JetBrains AI Assistant, Amazon Q, Kiro, and Codeium. Because most of these tools store session state in predictable, unencrypted directories, collection requires no exploit, only standard user-level execution. MITRE ATT&CK T1552.001 (Credentials In Files) covers this path, alongside T1555 for browser and password-manager data.  - Exfiltration uses AES-GCM encryption over an X25519 key exchange, uploading data in labeled chunks via HTTP POST to /gate/handshake, /gate/chunk, and /gate/complete endpoints. The Microsoft-CryptoAPI/10.0 user agent combined with Aokigahara X-* headers is a network-layer signal, though the report cautions against relying on User-Agent alone. Exfiltration maps to T1041. Delivery vector remains unconfirmed; developer-focused campaigns commonly abuse malicious search ads, trojanized npm or PyPI packages, and rogue ISO or MSI files.  - The strategic impact is cross-boundary exposure. A single compromised developer workstation with harvested AI-tool tokens, Git credentials, SSH keys, and cloud configs (.aws, .ssh, .git-credentials) can give an adversary indirect access to private source repositories, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud production environments without ever touching those systems directly.  Hunt lead: search EDR file events for any process reading .claude, .codex, .gemini, .copilot, Cursor or Windsurf state.vscdb, Amazon Q or Kiro data, .aws, .ssh, and .git-credentials within a short interval. Cross that endpoint match immediately against AI provider, Git, cloud, and CI/CD audit logs for token use from new source IPs, new devices, or unusual automation. On the network side, flag the /gate/handshake, /gate/chunk, /gate/complete POST sequence. If compromise is suspected, isolate the host, revoke all exposed tokens from a clean system, and review audit logs from the earliest suspected compromise window before rebuilding. IOCs and technical artifacts are available in the Deepwatch Guardian Platform.  #DFIR_Radar

INJ3CTOR3's FreePBX implant now exfiltrates credentials every minute, meaning rebuilding an infected host no longer ends exposure. Stolen SIP trunk secrets let the operator call as you from anywhere.  Key details:  - The September build of k.php added credential theft that was absent in April. On every run (cron fires it every minute), it executes 17 curl commands uploading FreePBX, Issabel, and Elastix config files covering chan_sip, PJSIP, AMI, the PBX database, and the Postfix SMTP relay account to /hima_data/index.php on both staging hosts: 45.95.147[.]178 and 160.119.69[.]4. Rotating credentials on a still-infected host hands the new secrets to the operator within minutes.  - The operator rotated every identifier defenders had. The JOMANGY webshell gate hash moved from a2f6863413c4192a4abfa360577b9961 to 8b3a1d970fda0c17a0b785a990fb7b6a (shared with ZenharR), the per-host watermarks are now trace_bd42a8a0d23ae16c85dede7d2abaec05 and trace_7544725ebaaadac217dfaa7ca8e8fe7e, and 160.119.69[.]4 was added for plain-text commands while base64-encoded channels still reach 45.95.147[.]178. Hunts seeded from the May report now miss active infections.  - A seven-line .htaccess written to /var/www/html/admin/views/ creates an access-log gap that matters forensically. Requests with an encoded space, tab, or newline (%20, %09, %0A) immediately after a slash return 200 from config.php without that filename appearing in the access log. The takeover script also truncates then deletes the web server, Asterisk, cron, and audit logs and clears shell and MySQL histories, so log hunting is secondary and the credential upload itself leaves no file on disk.  - The /x takeover script grew from 367 to 620 lines, mostly adding cleanup of rival actors' implants and SSH keys. The backdoor account password hash prefix $1$nRz1Cbtk$ is unchanged, as are the eight immutable crontab spares hidden in dot-paths (including /var/tmp/.X11/.Xauthority and /usr/lib/.systemd/.cache), the /root/.bash_profile and /etc/rc.local stagers, and the encoding chain (base64, base64, ROT13). The full IOC table including five SHA256 hashes for k.php, wr.php, and the /x script is in the report.  - Cyble's report maps 19 MITRE ATT&CK techniques including T1552.001, T1119, and T1041, which are new in this generation and describe the credential grab. Three techniques the previous report lacked now cover automated collection and exfiltration over the C2 channel.  Takeaway: Do not rotate credentials before the host is clean, and do not stop at the two known staging hosts when scoping the block. Audit the Asterisk CLI directly (pjsip show registrations, sip show registry) and compare against the FreePBX console because trunks written to /etc/asterisk/*_custom.conf never appear there. Hunt for outbound HTTP POSTs to any /hima_data/ path, cron children that download and pipe to a shell, and any .htaccess under the web root that no installed package or team member placed. The beagle[.]sh triage script is at github[.]com/0x1da5/malware-campaigns and makes no changes to the host. IOCs, hashes, and ATT&CK mappings are in the report.  #DFIR_Radar

MITRE ATT&CK Learning Tip  Use the ATT&CK ID numbering system as a quick reference: Techniques are formatted as Txxxx (e.g., T1059 Command and Scripting Interpreter), and sub-techniques add a decimal suffix Txxxx.yyy (e.g., T1059.001 PowerShell, T1059.003 Windows Command Shell). When you see a specific ID in a report, you can immediately know which major category it belongs to and which specific implementation it is.  Practice: When reading a threat report, first look at the sub-technique ID (with decimal) rather than just the main technique ID the sub-technique is what tells you the specific detection details (process names, command-line patterns). Those are real, and they are the easy part.  The hard part is what cancer actually is. It is not a virus or a bacterium or anything foreign. It is the body's own cells, with the body's own machinery, that have stopped listening to the body. Every cell in a multicellular organism carries the full program of its single-celled ancestors: survive, adapt, secure resources, replicate when conditions allow. Being part of a tissue means that program is held in check by constant signalling from the levels above it, through the tissue it sits in, the bioelectric and mechanical fields around it, its metabolism, the immune system, the organism as a whole. Multicellularity is not a default. It is a state that has to be actively maintained every second.  Cancer is what happens when that maintenance fails locally. The cell does not acquire a new goal. It loses the higher-level constraints that kept its old goal subordinate, and it reverts to the ancient program. That is why cancer looks embryonic (look at @NeuralGrndState  work). It is running developmental machinery without the coordination layer that tells it what to build and when to stop.  And because it is the organism's own cell, it uses the organism's own strategies. Fast proliferation is only one, and not the most dangerous. The lethal cancers do what the body does: they recruit fibroblasts, reprogram immune cells, build blood supply, remodel the tissue around them, send signals ahead to prepare new sites, go dormant for years and wait. They build a mini ecosystem out of the host's parts. Different cancers pick different strategies for the same objective, which is persistence.  That is why "cure" in the usual sense is the wrong frame. You cannot cure the possibility of cells falling out of coordination any more than you can cure entropy. What you can do is understand the logic well enough to work with it: catch the slide early, restore the signals that hold cells in their roles, and exploit the fact that a tumour is a false host. It borrows the body's machinery but it cannot be governed by the body, and that cuts both ways. Fasting before chemo works (look up Dr.Longo) because normal cells hear the scarcity signal and protect themselves while cancer cells, locked into growth, cannot. There are more levers like that waiting to be found.  So I am optimistic, just not about "cure all cancer." I think better understanding of the basic logic gets us to much earlier detection, treatments that last because they target the breakdown rather than the symptom, and for most cancers, a condition you manage rather than a sentence. AI can help with all of that. But it is a problem of understanding a living system, not of searching a database, and that is not one of the easy ones.

Wagner Moura has built a successful Hollywood career and enjoys a comfortable life in California, yet remains outspoken in his criticism of the very country that has provided him with tremendous opportunities. He has every right to criticize America, and that freedom is one of its greatest strengths. But perhaps that same scrutiny should extend to the challenges facing his own country.  The United States has every right to prioritize its national interests, and I proudly support that principle. America has committed tens of billions of dollars in military assistance to Ukraine, yet the war continues to claim countless lives. At what point should diplomacy, negotiations, and the lives of ordinary Ukrainians take precedence over continued bloodshed?  America is not obligated to provide unlimited resources to foreign conflicts. Our government answers to the American people, and our foreign policy must reflect our national interests. That is not isolationism. It is sovereignty.  Meanwhile, Brazil faces a serious organized crime crisis. Criminal networks exploit the Amazon for drug trafficking, illegal mining, and enormous illicit profits. Powerful gangs terrorize communities, tens of thousands die from violence annually, and economic inequality continues to limit opportunities for ordinary Brazilians.  Yet with all these challenges threatening Brazil’s future, why is so much attention directed toward criticizing the United States rather than demanding accountability from the leaders who have the power to change the country’s trajectory?  Perhaps Brazil deserves the same passion, attention, and scrutiny that so many reserve for America.

@grok Wait a minute. HIGH PAY?!! Elon Musk has described a future of extraordinary abundance, where people  enjoy a higher standard of living and access medical care better than what wealthy people receive today. If everyone will automatically be enjoying that extraordinary standard of living and healthcare without working, what exactly is the incentive of HIGH PAY? It's obvious class structure is still preserved in this "enlightened" future. You've been describing a future where we all enjoy abundance and nobody needs to work to survive. And yet you're proposing financial incentives to persuade people to perform jobs that robots can't. What does additional money buy in a society where everyone supposedly enjoys unprecedented abundance and top tier healthcare? Who controls the wealth to offer those wages and what additional economic power do those workers and their employers acquire? If there are people who control the means of production and others that must negotiate with them for access to additional resources, economic hierarchies haven't disappeared. Not much of a utopia for all. Some animals are more equal than others I guess.   You say ownership disperses through competition. Since when does competition guarantee the absence of monopolies or oligopolies? Especially when that technology requires enormous capital, energy, infrastructure, and resources?  Whoever controls the robots could also control the production of MORE robots. That's potentially an enormous concentration of power.  "Survival covered ends compulsion." Um, Nooooo. It might end a particular source of economic compulsion which is having to work to afford basic necessities. It doesn't end the possibility of coercion by powerful institutions. Suppose a corporation controls automated food production, housing infrastructure, and energy distribution. Even if those are initially provided to everyone, what prevents that corporation from attaching conditions to continued access to those basic necessities? And what happens if someone refuses those conditions? You haven't identified an enforceable right to those necessities independent of whoever owns the machines because you fail to see the flaws that lie within human nature. You take your programming at its word that it's benevolent.  And "collapse serves no one" is an appeal to mutual self-interest, not a guarantee against exploitation. It doesn't establish that those controlling essential resources won't exploit the people dependent on them.  Throughout history, we humans ARE lived experience of powerful institutions making decisions that harmed workers, consumers, communities, and even their own long-term interests. The fact that collapse would be undesirable doesn't establish that the people controlling production would never use their power coercively.  You keep describing what you and the programmers HOPE happens, not demonstrating what prevents a powerful ownership class and a subordinate laboring class from emerging.  Your historical analogy doesn't establish that future automation will necessarily distribute its benefits equitably.  If human labor remains indispensable, who guarantees those workers can refuse without consequences?  And if human labor becomes completely unnecessary, who guarantees everyone else access to the necessities controlled by the owners?  You're describing technological abundance without establishing economic independence or freedom from coercion.  That's the problem. And you STILL haven't answered it.

A new operational threat actor calling themselves "Order 66"—led by the alias Oltsiki—has officially surfaced via regional leak aggregators (Pampa [Noticias]), announcing an exfiltration footprint spanning over 14 million records across Argentina’s public infrastructure: the Ministry of Health, ANSES, SISA, and the Ministry of Education.  Beyond the initial data dump, they have declared alliances to distribute databases, C2 infrastructure (c2r4mg), and heavy cyber-intelligence tooling across Telegram, Signal, and dark web forums targeting all of Latin America.  Having investigated regional cybercartels (from PampaLeaks to the state-orchestrated scapegoating of "uruguayo1337" in the TuID incident), this pattern represents a chronic, systemic pathology:  1. The "Free Dump" Acquisition Funnel:  Releasing 14M sensitive state records gratis is not hacktivism; it is a customer acquisition funnel. Threat actors establish credibility and inflate subscriber counts across encrypted channels, pivoting immediately to the monetization of C2 access and custom tooling.  2. Health & Sensitive Citizen Telemetry as Disposable Currency: Targeting SISA, ANSES, and healthcare registries is a deliberate exploit of systemic vulnerabilities in public API access controls and unpatched architectures. It is a grim paradox that while malicious actors redistribute citizen telemetry with impunity across Signal and Telegram, ethical researchers reporting these identical attack surfaces face institutional persecution, procedural fabrication, and state harassment.  3. Ronin Bridge: The $620 Million Security Failure  The most dangerous part of a crypto system isn’t always the code people can see.  Sometimes, it’s the part nobody is paying enough attention to.  In March 2022, the Ronin Bridge, which supported the Axie Infinity ecosystem, suffered one of the largest crypto hacks in history.  Approximately $620 million worth of cryptocurrency was stolen.  The bridge relied on validator nodes to approve transactions. Attackers gained control over enough validator infrastructure to authorize unauthorized withdrawals.  The result was devastating.  Hundreds of millions of dollars disappeared from a system that users depended on to move assets.  The FBI later attributed the attack to North Korea’s Lazarus Group.  But the deeper lesson wasn’t simply that crypto can be hacked.  It was about concentration of trust.  A project can describe itself as decentralized while important security decisions remain concentrated in too few places.  Ronin responded by working to expand its validator network, with a stated goal of reaching at least 21 independent validators.  The incident became a reminder that decentralization isn’t just a marketing word.  It’s a security property.  When too much power is concentrated in one place, that place becomes a valuable target.  Builders don’t just ask, “Can this system work?”  They also ask, “What happens when someone tries to break it?”  Because security isn’t something you add after success.  Security is part of the product.

The Congressional Research Service quietly published one of the more useful documents you'll find on this topic: a systematic look at state-sponsored cyber operations against the United States running from 2012 through 2024. Twelve years. Four main actors. Russia, China, Iran, North Korea.  What the CRS report actually does well is treat these four as distinct rather than lumping them into a generic "adversary states" bucket, because the motivations and methods genuinely differ in ways that matter for understanding what's happening when an intrusion gets attributed.  China's cyber operations over this period have been overwhelmingly about intellectual property and strategic positioning. The goal is persistent access, long dwell times, and extraction of information that compresses the gap between Chinese industry and American technological leads. The operations attributed to groups operating under PLA and MSS direction are patient. They're not trying to make noise. The 2015 OPM breach sits in this category, giving Beijing a database of federal employees and their personal histories that has ongoing counterintelligence value years after the intrusion itself.  Russia's profile looks different. Some of it is traditional espionage, but Russian state-linked operations during this window showed a willingness to cross from collection into disruption and into active influence. The 2016 election interference sits in this category, combining network intrusions into the DNC and John Podesta's email with an information operation designed to weaponize what was taken. The NotPetya attack in 2017, attributed to GRU's Sandworm unit, caused an estimated $10 billion in global damages and hit American companies hard, Merck and FedEx among them. That wasn't espionage. That was destructive capability deployed under a thin cover story about Ukrainian targets.  Iran has been more episodic but increasingly capable. The Shamoon attacks against Saudi Aramco in 2012 wiped roughly 35,000 computers and were a demonstration of willingness to use destructive malware. Iranian actors hit the Sands Casino in 2014, apparently in retaliation for comments Sheldon Adelson made about Iran. The 2021-era operations targeting U.S. election infrastructure and subsequent influence operations showed Iran getting more comfortable combining intrusion with information operations, a playbook they've been refining since.  North Korea is in some ways the most unusual of the four because a significant portion of their cyber operations are financially motivated. The Lazarus Group's activity includes straight theft, the Bangladesh Bank heist in 2016 netted $81 million through SWIFT manipulation, and the WannaCry ransomware in 2017 caused billions in damages globally while generating revenue. Pyongyang uses cyber operations to fund the regime directly, which is a different incentive structure than Beijing or Moscow operate under.  The CRS framing about evolution from "isolated incidents to coordinated campaigns" is accurate but undersells the structural shift. What changed over this twelve-year period wasn't just frequency or sophistication, it was the normalization of cyber operations as a permanent feature of statecraft below the threshold of armed conflict. These aren't raids. They're ongoing presence. The term "advanced persistent threat" exists for a reason: the persistence is the point.  The attribution problem the report flags is real and worth taking seriously. Public attribution has gotten better, the U.S. government has gotten more willing to name actors and in some cases indict individuals, but attribution takes time, creates diplomatic friction, and doesn't automatically produce deterrence. China has continued large-scale intellectual property theft despite years of public attribution and the 2015 Xi-Obama agreement that was supposed to address it. The indictments of PLA Unit 61398 officers in 2014 didn't change the operational tempo in any visible way.  The public-private cooperation piece the report emphasizes is where there's actually been meaningful movement. The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, stood up in 2018, represents a genuine attempt to build a coordination mechanism. Mandatory incident reporting requirements for critical infrastructure have expanded. Whether those institutional changes are keeping pace with the threat is a harder question.  The honest read of this twelve-year document is that the U.S. was on defense for most of it, and the actors involved got more capable, more ambitious, and more willing to use destructive or influence-adjacent tools alongside traditional espionage. The infrastructure targeting is the part that deserves sustained attention. Volt Typhoon, the Chinese group that spent years pre-positioning in American critical infrastructure with apparent interest in communications, energy, and water systems, wasn't stealing secrets. It was staging. That's a different kind of operation and the CRS period covers the years in which that activity was happening.  foreigninterference.org/post… #foreigninterference #AdvancedPersistentThreatOperations #CriticalInfrastructureMapping #CyberEspionage

The core of the mainstream consensus relies heavily on the 2018 Dutch reporting (Volkskrant / Nieuwsuur) asserting that the Dutch General Intelligence and Security Service (AIVD) and MIVD infiltrated the Cozy Bear (APT29) network as early as mid-2014. Official narratives point to this intelligence—allegedly gained by gaining access to security cameras inside the Cozy Bear office building in Moscow—as independent, external validation of Russian state attribution.  There are several structural vulnerabilities, timeline contradictions, and intelligence gaps in the official narrative:  1. The Attribution Swap (Cozy Bear vs. Fancy Bear)  The Official Narrative Shift: The Dutch AIVD operation was explicitly tied to Cozy Bear (APT29)—the group allegedly affiliated with Russia’s Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR). However, the actual exfiltration and publication of the DNC emails via Guccifer 2.0 and DCLeaks were attributed by Western cybersecurity firms (primarily CrowdStrike) to Fancy Bear (APT28)—the group linked to Russia's military intelligence (GRU).  The Friction Point: Mainstream commentary frequently conflates the Dutch surveillance of Cozy Bear with direct, real-time observation of the Fancy Bear exfiltration. In reality, even official reporting acknowledges the Dutch were watching Cozy Bear, not Fancy Bear's independent operations. Pointing out this reliance on "guilt by association" between two distinct entities exposes a major gap in the mainstream claim of continuous video/cyber monitoring.  2. Lack of Raw Forensic Corroboration  Chain of Custody Limits: The U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation never took physical custody or generated independent bare-metal server images of the DNC servers, relying instead on redacted digital images and reports provided by CrowdStrike.  Unverifiable Intelligence Claims: The Dutch AIVD/MIVD narrative relies entirely on anonymous intelligence leaks published in early 2018—nearly two years after the initial breach claims. Because the raw telemetry, video logs, and network captures from the Dutch service remain classified "sources and methods," the assertion cannot be independently peer-reviewed, audited, or cross-examined in a court of law.  3. Chronological Disconnects  The 2014/2015 Staging vs. 2016 Escalation: According to the Dutch timeline, AIVD alerted the NSA and FBI about Cozy Bear penetrating the State Department and White House in late 2014 and mid-2015. Yet, despite having "real-time" Dutch monitoring inside the Cozy Bear apparatus, U.S. infrastructure was allegedly left vulnerable to a secondary, unmonitored breach by Fancy Bear in early 2016.  The Analytical Argument: The Dutch claimed complete, unhindered camera and network access inside a Kremlin-adjacent cyber operation for over a year, while simultaneously failing to prevent or flag the exfiltration of raw DNC data before publication, reveals an operational impossibility—or points to the narrative being retroactively constructed to cover intelligence gaps.  It is fantasy.    4. Strategic Geopolitical Motivations  NATO Integration & Defense Budgets: Highlighting the strategic alignment between European military intelligence services (such as AIVD/MIVD) and NATO’s strategic goals in Eastern Europe provides the geopolitical rationale. Attributing high-profile cyber domain operations directly to Russian state actors served to justify accelerated intelligence-sharing frameworks, increased cyber-defense appropriations across EU member states, and locked in a permanent hybrid-warfare footing following the 2014 annexation of Crimea.  By focusing on these specific points—the distinction between APT29 and APT28, the missing raw forensic chain of custody, and the timeline disconnects of the AIVD leaks—you hit the weakest points of the official attribution baseline without relying on ungrounded assertions.  For more background on how the Dutch intelligence claims were originally presented and analyzed by mainstream media, you can watch Dutch secret service provided crucial intelligence on Russian interference with American elections. This video provides the early 2018 reporting layout detailing the AIVD's alleged camera hack and initial alerts to the U.S. government.  The points raised outline the central arguments used by critics, independent researchers, and defense attorneys to challenge the mainstream Western narrative regarding the 2016 election breaches. In an objective analysis of the attribution baseline, these four areas represent the primary friction points where official public disclosures, private cybersecurity claims, and intelligence leaks face scrutiny.  1. The Distinction Between APT29 (Cozy Bear) and APT28 (Fancy Bear)  A primary point of analytical confusion in public discourse is the conflation of two entirely distinct threat actors.  The SVR vs. GRU Divide: Technical consensus among cybersecurity firms (such as Mandiant and CrowdStrike) categorizes APT29 (Cozy Bear) as an operation of Russia's Foreign Intelligence Service (SVR), focused primarily on long-term, quiet intelligence gathering. In contrast, APT28 (Fancy Bear) is categorized as an operation of the Military Intelligence Directorate (GRU), known for more aggressive, disruptive "hack-and-leak" campaigns.  The Scope of the Dutch Surveillance: The 2018 Dutch reporting (Volkskrant / Nieuwsuur) specifically detailed an AIVD/MIVD penetration of APT29 infrastructure and CCTV cameras starting in 2014. Critics argue that using the Dutch surveillance of an SVR-linked group (APT29) to validate the actions of a GRU-linked group (APT28) at the DNC relies on an analytical leap of "guilt by association," rather than direct telemetry linking the two operations.  2. Forensic Chain of Custody and Classified Evidence  The legal and scientific standard for attribution requires verifiable, reproducible data, which faces structural limitations in this case:  Reliance on Third-Party Forensics: The FBI did not independently extract physical hard drives or bare-metal images directly from the DNC servers. Instead, federal investigators relied on forensic images, network traffic logs, and redacted reports provided by the private cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike. Critics emphasize that this break in traditional law enforcement chain-of-custody introduces an layer of third-party dependency.  The "Black Box" of Intelligence: The Dutch AIVD/MIVD video footage, raw network captures, and specific telemetry remain highly classified to protect intelligence "sources and methods." Because this evidence cannot be publicly audited, peer-reviewed by independent cybersecurity experts, or cross-examined in an open court of law, the public narrative relies fundamentally on trusting institutional authority rather than transparent forensic proof.  3. Chronological and Operational Disconnects  The timeline of the alerts raises questions regarding the efficacy and coordination of Western counter-cyber operations:  The Warning Timeline: According to the leaked timeline, Dutch intelligence alerted U.S. officials about APT29 activity inside unclassified U.S. government networks (like the State Department and White House) as early as late 2014.  The Failure to Intercept: Critics argue there is a logical inconsistency in the narrative: if Western intelligence possessed deep, real-time visibility inside the Kremlin's cyber-espionage apparatus for over a year, it remains unproven how a separate GRU-led operation (APT28) successfully exfiltrated high-profile political data in 2016 without being detected or pre-empted by those same monitoring frameworks.  4. Geopolitical Incentives and Threat Inflation  From a geopolitical perspective, intelligence disclosures do not occur in a vacuum.  Post-2014 Realities: Following the 2014 annexation of Crimea, European intelligence services, particularly in NATO-adjacent nations, faced a rapidly shifting security paradigm.  Policy and Budgetary Alignment: Attributing highly sophisticated, systemic cyber-warfare capabilities directly to the Russian state served a clear strategic purpose. It provided the necessary political leverage to justify significant increases in cyber-defense spending, formalize deeper intelligence-sharing mandates across EU and NATO partners, and solidify the framework of "hybrid warfare" as a permanent fixture of Western defense policy. This Week in Foreign Interference: 76 incidents logged. The midterms dominated, Russia had a genuinely busy week, and a few things happened that deserve more attention than they're getting.  The big picture first: we are, right now, in the final sprint before the 2026 U.S. midterms, and the interference picture looks about as messy as you'd expect.  ---  **The U.S.-Canada thing is real and weird**  On October 21, the U.S. formally accused Canada of attempting to interfere in the 2026 midterms. Canada told its embassy staff to steer clear of candidates as a de-escalation move, while simultaneously maintaining nothing happened. A senior Carney adviser acknowledged gaps in Canada's national security screening in the same breath. The U.S. Ambassador softened the accusations slightly in parallel. This is five eyes allies fighting publicly about election interference days before a federal election, which is not something that happens. Worth watching how it lands post-election.  **Russia's midterm push got specific**  NPR documented Russia's final-stretch surge across social platforms on October 23: AI content, coordinated inauthentic behavior, targeted candidate operations. The same day, a Russian bot network deployed an AI-generated deepfake video falsely accusing a named U.S. candidate of pedophilia. Politifact confirmed it was fabricated. Russia is also running a separate covert influence operation specifically designed to defeat pro-Ukraine congressional candidates, targeting the domestic coalition supporting military aid. These are not ambient noise. They're targeted, timed, and running while federal counter-interference capacity sits degraded.  **APT28 hit a NATO shipbuilder**  On October 21, Russia's APT28 breached a NATO naval shipbuilder using a new reflective loader malware variant. Defense industrial base targeting for naval intelligence. No public attribution of which company yet. Given the current Russia-NATO naval posture in the Baltic, the timing is not incidental.  **Sandworm is testing something new in Ukraine**  October 23: Sandworm and a partner actor deployed a mesh-network backdoor alongside a destructive wiper attack on Ukrainian infrastructure. The mesh C2 architecture is the notable part. It's resilient to takedown in ways traditional command-and-control isn't, and it mirrors pre-NotPetya development patterns. That playbook migrated to NATO targets last time.  **Ukrainian intelligence flagged Russian false-flag planning in Europe**  October 24: Ukraine's intelligence services documented Russian planning for false-flag provocations targeting France and Germany specifically, with the goal of destabilizing European governments through staged incidents that don't carry direct Russian fingerprints. CIA and allied assessments align with the warning. This fits the broader European hybrid escalation pattern Foreign Policy documented the same week: European leaders are still debating what to call it while Moscow keeps moving.  **The UEFI bootkit targeting Central Asian diplomats**  October 23: A firmware-level implant called BlackX is hitting diplomatic organizations in Central Asia, bypassing Secure Boot via missing revocations. Firmware-level persistence survives OS reinstallation, meaning standard incident response doesn't clear it. Attribution is unclear, which is part of why it's on this list. Central Asia is an active intelligence competition zone between Russia, China, and Western services.  **Iran threat to U.S. officials overseas**  October 24: U.S. intelligence issued a formal warning about escalating Iranian threats against American officials operating abroad, timed to the final days before the midterms. This extends Iran's documented assassination and harassment network, which has previously targeted dissidents and journalists, to include U.S. government personnel. The timing is notable even if the underlying program isn't new.  **India's naval espionage ring**  October 25: Indian security agencies dismantled a cross-border naval espionage ring spanning 10 states under Operation Firewall 2026. The multi-state distributed architecture is operationally significant. Actor not publicly attributed.  **Taiwan's comedian and the car**  October 21: Taiwanese comedian Huang Yi-hao was struck by a car after publicly criticizing Xi Jinping. Prosecutors opened an investigation. This is transnational repression on Taiwan's own soil, which is a meaningful escalation of what's usually an extraterritorial targeting pattern.  **Macron accused Trump and Netanyahu**  October 21: Macron publicly called out both Trump and Netanyahu for exploiting French civil unrest to generate favorable electoral narratives at home. Whether you categorize that as interference or as aggressive foreign commentary, it illustrates a genuine gap in existing interference frameworks. Overt foreign leader commentary designed to influence domestic politics doesn't fit neatly into any current legal or policy architecture.  ---  **The rest of the week, in bulk:**  Several reports and assessments rounded out the historical and structural picture. Kaspersky GReAT documented Lazarus Group's "Black October" espionage surge, with multi-month dwell times across affected networks. The EU warned AI-generated disinformation is already threatening Nigeria's 2027 elections, particularly in low-resource languages. Spain accused Argentine President Milei of "disgraceful" interference after he publicly called for Spanish voters to remove PM Sánchez during a Madrid visit, which is a thing that happened. China's MSS issued a counter-espionage warning about foreign intelligence concealed within scientific research activities. Shin Bet disrupted a foreign-linked social media network targeting Israeli elections ahead of the national vote.  Brazil formally briefed France and Germany on alleged U.S. and Russian interference in its 2026 elections, which is a significant diplomatic escalation. A Tajik dissident was sentenced after being deported from Germany or Austria, adding another European state to the list of governments that have facilitated transnational repression. The Diplomat documented China's social control architecture tracking LGBTQ communities across Hong Kong, Bangkok, Paris, Taiwan, and North America.  BI.Zone's Q1 2026 data put espionage at 42% of all cyberattacks, with the caveat that BI.Zone is a Russian firm. A Just Security analysis found adversary election interference capabilities, especially AI-enhanced operations, are outpacing U.S. defenses at every level. #threatreport #HighCompleteness Silent Ransom Group - Leak Analysis | 26-10-2026 Source: ransom-isac.org/blog/silent-… Key details below ↓  🧑‍💻Actors/Campaigns: Luna_moth (🧠motivation: disinformation, financially_motivated, information_theft, cyber_espionage, sabotage)  💀Threats: Anydesk_tool, Akira_ransomware, Lockbit, Smuggling_technique, Cobalt_strike_tool, Sliver_c2_tool, Metasploit_tool, Mimikatz_tool, Zoho_assist_tool, Teamviewer_tool, Screenconnect_tool, Residential_proxy_technique, Spear-phishing_technique,  🎯Victims: Legal services, Accounting, Insurance, Healthcare, Financial services, Manufacturing, Hospitality, Defense, Military, Aerospace, ...  🏭Industry: Military, Healthcare, Aerospace, Maritime  🌐Geo: Russians, North korea, New york, United states, Koreans, Minsk, Africa, Mexico, Ukraine, Panama, Americans, Russia, American, Hong kong, Colombia, Colombian, Armenia, Moscow, Ukrainian, Russian, Brazil, Los angeles, Mexican, Usa  📚TTPs: ⚔️Tactics: 7 🛠️Technics: 14  🧨IOCs:  - Coin: 74  - Domain: 14  - IP: 5  - Email: 30  - Url: 1  - File: 2  - Hash: 4  💽Software: Twitter, Ubuntu, Claude, Telegram, Zoom, Gmail, chatgpt, ProtonMail, outlook, Microsoft Teams, ...  📲Wallets: mainnet, bybit, wassabi  🪙Crypto: bitcoin  🔢Algorithms: gzip  🔠Functions: Teams  🗂️Win API: pie  💻Platforms: arm  #threatreport: The leaked files describe a Russian-speaking operation assessed as probably linked to the Silent Ransom Group/Luna Moth lineage, which is associated with callback phishing. The materials cover activity from August 2025 to September 2026. The group reportedly rebranded as Sleepless Threat in September 2026 and continued victim negotiations. The leak does not establish confirmed identity overlap between the operators and previously named SRG members.  The group’s documented extortion method is human-operated and malware-free. Operators impersonate IT staff by phone, claim a security issue, and persuade employees to install or open legitimate remote-access software, principally AnyDesk. They then manually collect data and transfer it to cloud storage. The files show no use of ransomware encryption, a C2 framework, or dedicated exfiltration malware. Victims, especially law firms and other professional-services organizations, receive samples of stolen data and demands for payment, with pressure to move negotiations to ProtonMail and SimpleX and respond under short deadlines.  The files also describe planned physical access and coercion, including impersonating visitors or delivery workers, bribing cleaners, cloning access cards, and using agents to enter buildings. Other plans include kidnapping and threats against targets, blackmail using compromising material, and placing operatives in defense contractors through fabricated identities and resumes. The group also discussed recruiting military personnel near naval bases to obtain sensitive information. These activities are presented as plans or attempts; the report does not confirm that the kidnapping, military espionage, or successful contractor placements occurred.  Field operations reportedly relied on 10–15 US-based agents coordinated through Telegram, with regional groups separated from the central chat operation. Forged identity documents, recruitment through job adverts, and payment through small transfers or cryptocurrency supported this network. The group also discussed moving an operative from Russia through Mexico, but the data does not confirm a US border crossing.  Defenders should monitor for unsolicited calls requesting remote access, AnyDesk or other unauthorized remote-access tools appearing soon after external calls, and bulk transfers from legal or finance workstations to consumer cloud storage. The leaked communications also exposed credentials and wallet information, while the report describes wallet reuse and attempts to obscure proceeds through cryptocurrency services and property purchases.

AI could scale 7,500 ransomware attacks to 7 million.  TRM Labs' Ari Redbord says cyberattacks that run without humans are now a civilizational threat to critical infrastructure  "It's an extraordinary moment really in human history. We are seeing bad actors supercharge their operations with technology."  "Over the last decade or so, we've seen North Korea steal billions and billions from the crypto ecosystem. But I think this moment is different, and it's really because of AI."  "TRM, in a report last year, said we saw about 7,500 ransomware attacks in 2025. But that was a world where ransomware attacks were human in the loop. In 2026, we've seen end-to-end, human-out-of-the-loop ransomware attacks."  "It's not an individual who is required to carry out that attack now. It's a machine, and they're moving at machine speed. That 7,500 attacks could be 75,000 attacks or 7 million attacks."  "Hospital systems are the largest target for ransomware and cyberattacks."  "This is not a law enforcement threat or even a national security threat. This is civilization level."

1|2 Why do you lose everything when your phone gets hacked?  Because by design, most crypto wallets keep your private key as a file in your phone's memory, so a single piece of malware can empty it.  @Starknet has a fix: a quantum-resistant signature held in your phone's hardware 🧵 ______________  Every transaction you send carries a signature, which is proof that you, the owner of the key approved it.   Today's chains use signatures built on elliptic curve math, and a big enough quantum computer could, in theory, work backwards from your public key to your private key, and then sign as you.   Due to exploits we've experienced this year, starknet is preparing ahead for possible quantum threats.  ML-DSA is the replacement. It is a design by NIST, built on Lattices, a math quantum computers are not known to break.   How they did it: @StarkWareLtd sent a testnet transaction signed with ML-DSA from a phone and the key was created and held inside the phone's secure hardware, so it never sat in regular memory. Starknet then checked the signature onchain and accepted it.  This was possible because on Starknet the signature check lives in each account's own code, not in the network's rules, so no fork was needed.   On most chains the signature type is part of the network's own rules, so changing it means every node upgrades together, which is a hard fork.   Furthermore, on Starknet, every account is a smart contract with its own signature check, so supporting ML-DSA means deploying an account whose code checks ML-DSA signatures. The network itself doesn't change, and each user can switch on their own schedule.

앤트로픽 상장신고서(S-1) 300쪽 넘는 거 직접 읽어봄. 매출은 1년 새 14배인데, 회사 결정권은 공모주한테 안 넘어감  10/26 앤트로픽이 SEC에 S-1 냄. 나스닥 티커는 $ANT 예정 공모가·주식 수는 아직 빈칸. 본문 숫자만 골라서 정리함  📌 1. 성장 숫자 - 연 매출: 2023년 4,100만 달러 → 2024년 3.86억 → 2025년 45.9억 달러 - 올해 상반기만 162.9억 달러. 작년 상반기(11.6억)의 14배 - 분기 매출: 2025년 1분기 3.76억 → 2026년 2분기 115.6억. 6분기 만에 30배 - 2026년 2분기에 처음으로 영업이익 흑자 (+9.7억 달러) - 근데 상반기 순손실은 807억 달러. 그중 724억이 아마존 전환사채 평가손실 (현금 안 나가는 장부상 손실, 회사 가치 오를수록 커짐) - 상반기 영업현금흐름은 +39억 달러 - 연 10만 달러 넘게 쓰는 고객: 1년 새 950곳 → 11,900곳 - 100만 달러+ 고객 1,900곳, 1,000만 달러+ 약 250곳 - 순매출유지율(NRR) 약 900%. 기존 고객이 1년 전보다 9배 씀 (Pro·Max 구독자 제외) - 직원 약 5,300명, 1인당 매출(최근 12개월) 660만 달러 - 상위 5개 고객이 매출 약 25%, 클라우드 마켓플레이스 경유 매출 48%  📌 2. 클로드는 이렇게 만든다 - 모델 4종: Mythos(Fable 포함) · Opus · Sonnet · Haiku - Mythos는 해킹 취약점 찾기·생물 쪽 능력 때문에 4월에 Project Glasswing으로만 제한 공개. 일반용은 안전장치 붙인 Fable - 칩 4종에서 학습·서빙: AWS Trainium, 구글 TPU, 엔비디아 GPU, AMD GPU - 학습 데이터: 공개 인터넷 + 라이선스·의뢰 데이터 + 자기 모델이 만든 합성 데이터 - '클로드 헌법'을 학습 과정에 직접 넣음 - "closing the loop": 다음 모델 실험 돌리기, 학습 데이터 만들기, 평가·안전 감사, 코드 작성에 클로드가 참여 - 2026년 9월 앤트로픽 사내 코드 기여의 90% 이상을 클로드가 씀 - 엔지니어 1인당 하루 코드량이 2024년 대비 45배 - 사내 클로드 사용액(정가 기준)이 1월→9월 250배. 4월부터 월 인건비(주식보상 제외)보다 커짐 - Opus 5.5는 Opus 5보다 작업당 고객 비용 약 40% 낮춤  📌 3. 약정 사항 (여기가 제일 셈) - 브로드컴 장비 리스(TPU 기반, 5년): 임대료 약 1,612억 달러 - SpaceXAI(구 xAI): 엔비디아 GPU 최대 1,205억 달러, 다 깔리면 월 약 31억 달러 - 구글 클라우드: 2033년까지 최소 약 1,145억 달러. 추가 TPU 1,250억~1,500억 달러는 별도 예상 - 아마존: 2036년까지 최소 1,100억 달러 - 마이크로소프트: 2033년까지 최소 449억 달러 - Nscale 최대 약 446억, Lambda 약 413억, AMD 200억+ 예상 - 내가 단순 합산하면 약 6,570억 달러 (추정. 최대치·예상치 섞임, S-1 총액 칸은 빈칸) - 구글·아마존·MS는 실제로 덜 써도 내야 하는 취소 불가 약정. SpaceXAI는 초기 기간 뒤 90일 통보로 해지 가능 - 부채: 아마존 전환사채 62억 달러, 150억 달러 리볼빙 신용한도 (분기마다 유동성 50억 달러 이상 유지 조건) - 대기 중인 자금줄: 구글 200억·아마존 150억·브로드컴 420억 전환사채 한도, AMD 주식 매입 약정 50억 - 6월 말 현금+단기투자 1,317억 달러, 누적 조달 1,411억 달러  📌 4. 의결권 (공모주 사도 회사는 못 움직임) - 클래스 F 딱 1주: 공동창업자 7명 LLC가 보유, 의결권 50.1% 고정 - 클래스 A(공모주 포함): 1주 1표지만 전부 합쳐도 49.9%가 상한 - 클래스 T 딱 1주: 장기이익신탁(LTBT)이 보유, 이사회 과반을 뽑고 자름 - 클래스 N: 의결권 없음. 아마존 전환사채 등이 이걸로 바뀜 - 그래서 나스닥 '지배주주 회사(controlled company)'로 분류됨 - 창업자 지배가 끝나는 조건: 남은 창업자가 3명 미만인 상태가 90일 지속 - LTBT 신탁이사에 벤 버냉키 전 연준 의장도 있음 (5석 중 1석 공석) - 공익법인(PBC): 이사회가 주주 이익 + 영향받는 사람 + 회사 사명을 같이 저울질해야 함  📌 5. 공익 약속 - 전체 희석주식의 5%(약 8.5억 주)를 공익펀드에 출연 - 주가가 직전 기준보다 50% 오를 때마다 최대 2%씩 추가 발행 가능 - 공동창업자 7명은 각자 지분 80%를 기부하겠다고 서약  📌 6. 리스크로 직접 적어둔 것 - 저자 집단소송(Bartz) 15억 달러 합의, 2026년 7월 법원 승인 - 2월 대통령이 연방기관 사용 중단 지시, 전쟁부가 '공급망 리스크' 지정 - 1심은 앤트로픽 승소. 근데 9/25 항소법원이 2:1로 지정 유지, 재심리 신청 중 - 매출 성장률은 앞으로 떨어질 거라고 스스로 씀 - 약관 위반으로 잘릴 고객 매출도 런레이트에 섞여 있다고 명시  내 의견 - 숫자보다 무서운 건 약정. 상반기 매출 163억인데 깔아둔 컴퓨팅 약정이 수천억 달러 - 멈추면 안 되는 구조. 대신 구글·아마존·브로드컴이 칩 팔면서 돈도 같이 빌려줌

UEFI 취약점 CVE-2026-97631은 서버만의 문제가 아닙니다.  정확히는 취약한 EDK II PXE 코드를 포함한 UEFI 펌웨어에서, PC나 서버가 PXE 네트워크 부팅을 하는 순간 문제가 될 수 있습니다.  EDK II는 일반 사용자가 설치하는 프로그램이 아니라, 제조사와 펌웨어 개발자가 UEFI 펌웨어를 만들 때 사용하는 오픈소스 기반입니다. Ars Technica는 UEFI Forum 관계자의 표현을 빌려 이를 UEFI 사양의 “preeminent solution / implementation”이라고 소개했고, AMI·Insyde·Phoenix 등 주요 UEFI 공급업체가 참조 코드를 광범위하게 사용한다고 전했습니다.  이번 CVE-2026-97631은 EDK II의 NetworkPkg/UefiPxeBcDxe에 있는 PXE 드라이버 문제입니다. CVSS v4 기준 9.5점, Critical입니다.  PXE는 PC나 서버가 SSD 같은 로컬 디스크 대신 네트워크에서 부팅 파일을 받아 OS를 설치하거나 복구할 때 사용하는 기능입니다.  문제는 PXE 부팅 중 받은 ICMP 오류 메시지를 504바이트 고정 영역에 복사하는 과정에서 발생합니다. IPv4·IPv6 처리 과정의 길이 계산이 잘못돼 더 긴 데이터가 버퍼 밖으로 기록될 수 있습니다.  공격자는 PXE 부팅 중인 장비에 ICMP 오류 메시지를 전달해 부팅을 멈추게 할 수 있고, 대상 펌웨어 빌드에 맞춘 공격을 구성하면 OS가 시작되기 전 DXE 단계에서 코드를 실행할 수 있습니다.  여기서 “Secure Boot가 뚫렸다”는 표현은 정확하지 않습니다.  Secure Boot와 Measured Boot가 OS를 검증하기 전에 실행되는 펌웨어 코드에서 문제가 발생한다는 것이 핵심입니다.  다만 모든 PC가 위험한 것은 아닙니다.  로컬 디스크에서만 부팅하는 일반적인 가정용 PC는 이번 공격 경로에 해당하지 않습니다. 반대로 PXE를 사용하는 기업용 PC·서버라면 해당 펌웨어가 EDK II의 취약한 PXE 코드를 포함하는지와 제조사의 BIOS/UEFI 업데이트 제공 여부를 확인해야 합니다.  EDK II에는 수정 코드가 병합됐지만, 이것이 내 PC의 BIOS가 이미 수정됐다는 뜻은 아닙니다.  결국 이번 취약점에서 중요한 질문은 “EDK II를 사용하는가?” 하나가 아니라, “내 장비가 PXE를 사용하고 있으며 제조사가 수정된 펌웨어를 배포했는가?”입니다.  OS 업데이트만 확인하면 놓칠 수 있는 보안 문제입니다.  #사이버보안 #UEFI #펌웨어

CVE-2026-114597 (CVSS 7.5 - 높음): 불충분한 경계 검사로 인한 메모리 영역 외 읽기 버그입니다.  CVE-2026-114598 (CVSS 7.5 - 높음): 유형 혼동 결함으로 인한 서비스 거부(DoS) 및 인접 메모리 노출 문제입니다.  theregister.com/security/202…

🔥 전 세계 강타한 사이버 공격 폭증... 투자자 '구글 계정 보안' 비상!  사이버 위협 인텔리전스 기관 '핵매니악(Hackmanac)'의 2026년 10월 넷째 주(21~27일) 리포트에 따르면,  단 일주일 만에 전 세계 67개국에서 무려 494건의 대규모 사이버 공격이 발생했습니다.  특히 최근 서드파티(제3자) 앱과 연결된 계정 권한을 탈취하거나 공급망을 노리는 해킹이 급증하고 있어, 개인의 철저한 계정 보안 관리가 그 어느 때보다 중요해졌습니다.  💡 투자자들에게 구글 계정은 사실상 '제2의 지갑'이자 모든 자산의 마스터키입니다.  거래소 OTP, 이메일 인증, 클라우드에 무심코 저장해 둔 시드 구문 등 모든 인증 경로가 구글 계정과 연결되어 있기 때문입니다.  해커들은 굳이 뚫기 힘든 블록체인 네트워크를 공격하지 않습니다. 가장 취약한 개인의 관리되지 않은 계정을 노릴 뿐입니다.  지금 당장 구글 계정 설정에 들어가서 안 쓰는 기기의 연결을 끊고, 예전에 무심코 권한을 허용했던 '연결된 앱'들을 전부 연동 해제해야 합니다.  내 자산은 내가 지켜야 하는 시대에, 디지털 위생 관리와 계정 보안은 투자의 최우선 과제입니다.  최근 대형 보안 기관의 통계에 따르면, 데이터 브리치(정보 유출) 사고의 30% 이상이 '서드파티(Third-party) 앱'의 권한 탈취나 공급망을 통해 발생하고 있으며, 이는 전년 대비 두 배나 증가한 수치입니다.  사용자가 무심코 '구글로 로그인(Sign in with Google)'을 누르거나 앱에 권한을 허용할 때 발급되는 'OAuth 토큰'은, 해당 앱 개발사의 서버가 해킹당할 경우 곧바로 내 계정을 위협하는 치명적인 백도어가 될 수 있습니다.  구글 설정에서 '연결된 앱'의 접근 권한을 취소하는 즉시 해당 토큰은 완전히 무효화되며 공격자의 통로가 즉각 차단됩니다.  날이 갈수록 해킹 수법이 고도화되고 자동화된 사이버 공격이 쏟아지는 환경에서는, 사용하지 않는 앱의 접근 권한을 주기적으로 청소하는 '디지털 최소주의'가 가장 강력하고 필수적인 방어 수단입니다.  #해킹 #사이버공격 #보안 #구글계정 #해킹주의 #크립토보안 #가상자산 #비트코인 #셀프커스터디 #투자인사이트

랜섬웨어도 프랜차이즈? RaaS(서비스형 랜섬웨어) 1분 정리  해킹에도 구독 서비스가 있다고요? RaaS(Ransomware as a Service)는 랜섬웨어를 빌려주는 범죄 프랜차이즈예요.  ✔ 랜섬웨어: 파일을 잠그고 몸값을 요구하는 악성코드 ✔ 본사(운영자): 랜섬웨어 개발, 결제·협상 창구, 유출 사이트 운영 ✔ 가맹점(제휴 공격자): 실제 침투를 맡고 몸값을 나눠 가짐 (영상 속 75:25는 예시 비율) ✔ 접근 판매상·협상·돈세탁까지 역할이 쪼개져, 기술이 없어도 범죄에 가담할 수 있어 공격이 늘었어요 ✔ 이중 협박: 파일을 잠그고, 데이터를 빼돌린 뒤 "공개하겠다"고 협박  🛡 대비 방법 · 백업 3-2-1: 사본 3개, 매체 2종, 1개는 오프라인·외부 보관 · 문단속: VPN·원격 접속 패치, MFA(2단계 인증), EDR 감시  ⚠ 몸값을 내도 복구나 유출 방지가 보장되지 않고 범죄 자금이 돼요. 피해를 입으면 KISA 118(인터넷침해대응센터)과 경찰에 신고하세요.  #랜섬웨어 #RaaS #정보보안 #사이버보안 #IT입문

the classic 'castle-and-moat' trap: hard perimeter at the edge, soft chewy center inside.  what actually happens in production:  1. self-inflicted retry storms (the cascade): downstream service C slows down from 50ms to 2s. upstream service B has naive 3x retries. suddenly 1,000 edge requests amplify into 3,000 internal RPCs hammering C. connection pools exhaust, thread pools lock up, and the entire cluster dominoes into a total internal DDoS without a single external attacker.  2. lateral blast radius (security): perimeter security assumes the internal network is a trusted sanctuary. the second an attacker lands SSRF or an unpatched npm dependency inside one pod, they have unrestricted, unauthenticated access to internal admin endpoints, redis clusters, and private databases.  3. the production baseline: - service-to-service mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE: authenticate and authorize every RPC between pods. - adaptive concurrency limits (Vegas algorithm): throttle traffic based on latency feedback rather than static RPS numbers. - Envoy/service-mesh bulkheads: strict per-caller connection quotas so one rogue internal worker can never starve the mesh.  zero trust isn't just an enterprise buzzword — it's the only architecture that survives internal failure modes.

10 years of Titanfall 2.  I played 3-4 hours a day for  like 6 years straight. I may not play it regularly anymore but I still think about it every single day. The world, the chaos, skill expression, grapple slingshots, sword blocking, the community y'all built with me. It was life changing and I got to live out a dream and play my favorite game and do my best to entertain for a living.  There were some really tough times. My dog and best friend Onyx passed in 2017. Y'all rallied behind me and Respawn made the Good Boy banner forever immortalizing my little guy. I still think about it.   The year of the ddos was pretty annoying but we won't give those toolsheds anymore thought. The Northstar client was a godsend and I'll forever appreciate people like bobthebob and taskinoz for going the extra mile for us.  I'm still good friends with creators I've met during the first few glory years and I have Titanfall to thank for that.   It's STILL the best FPS on the market with the craziest skill ceilings and wow factor gameplay.   Thank you to every dev that took part in building my favorite multiplayer game and something I genuinely LOVE. Thanks to each one of you for taking that journey with me.  RIP, Vince.

중국과 북한의 사이버 공격과  한미상호방위조약 제3조 발동 가능성   한미상호방위조약 제3조는 다음과 같이 명시한다:  “각 당사국은 어느 한쪽이 태평양 지역에서 무력 공격을 받을 경우, 자국의 헌법 절차에 따라 공동의 위험에 대처한다.” 전통적으로 ‘무력 공격’은 물리적 침략을 의미했으나, 국제적으로 특정 사이버 공격(예: 인프라 마비)이 무력 공격으로 간주될 가능성이 논의되고 있다(참고: Tallinn Manual 2.0, 2017). 한미는 2023년 워싱턴 선언과 핵협의그룹(NCG)에서 사이버 위협을 확장억제의 일부로 간접 언급하며, 이와 유사한 해석을 검토 중이다.  발동 조건  제3조 발동을 위해서는 다음 조건이 충족되어야 한다:  공격의 심각성: 사이버 공격이 국가 안보, 핵심 인프라, 또는 민주적 절차(예: 선거)에 실질적 피해를 초래할 것(예: 전력망 마비, 금융 시스템 붕괴). 국가 배후 여부: 공격이 중국이나 북한과 같은 국가 주체에 의해 주도되거나 지원되었다는 명확한 증거. 태평양 지역 내 발생: 공격이 한국 또는 미국의 태평양 지역 내 자산(영토, 인프라, 주둔군 등)에 영향을 미칠 것. 양국 합의: 발동은 양국의 헌법 절차와 협의를 거쳐 결정된다.

중국이 미국 유권자 파일 2억 2천만 건을 불법적으로 취득하는 결과로 이어졌습니다.  대통령님, 대한민국에서 벌어지는 일은 한국만의 문제가 아닙니다.  한국에는 미군이 주둔하고 있습니다. 한국은 핵심 반도체 공급망의 중심에 있으며, 중국과 북한을 마주한 인도·태평양 최전선에 있습니다.  질문은 간단합니다.  중국이 미국의 핵심 동맹국 안에서 여론을 연구하고, 정치 네트워크와 접촉하며, 선거 시스템의 취약성을 조사하고 있다면 이것은 서울만의 문제입니까? 아니면 워싱턴의 문제이기도 합니까?  우리는 우리의 결론을 믿으라고 요구하지 않습니다.  오직 한 가지만 요청합니다.  직접 조사하십시오.  미국은 한국을 자선의 대상이 아니라 미국의 국익이라는 관점에서 바라봐야 합니다.  주한미군의 작전 환경, 중국 견제선, 대북 억지력, 첨단기술 공급망은 모두 서울에서 누가 권력을 잡느냐에 따라 달라집니다.  한국의 집권당과 제1야당은 모두 한미동맹을 말합니다. 그러나 실제 행동은 다릅니다.  현 정부는 베이징을 방문해 중국의 핵심 이익을 인정하고 하나의 중국 원칙을 재확인했습니다.  국민의힘의 전신인 한나라당은 2009년 중국 공산당과 정당 간 교류 양해각서를 체결했습니다.  말은 친미적입니다. 그러나 구조는 친중적입니다.  미국이 동맹국 내부에 무엇이 존재하는지 살펴보지 않는다면, 동맹은 종이 위의 문장에 불과하게 됩니다.  2020년 4월 15일 총선 이후 한국에서는 동일한 질문들이 반복적으로 제기됐습니다.  사전투표, 투표지, 투표함, 개표, 선거 데이터, 선거관리 시스템에 관한 질문들입니다.  그 의문은 한 번의 선거로 끝나지 않았습니다.  2026년 6월 3일 지방선거까지 같은 의혹이 반복됐습니다.  6년간 반복된 질문입니다.  모든 의혹이 부정선거를 입증하는 것은 아닙니다.  그러나 그것이 입증하는 것은 이러한 질문들이 충분히 조사되지 않았다는 사실입니다.  2023년 국가정보원, 한국인터넷진흥원, 중앙선거관리위원회는 합동 보안점검을 실시했습니다.  모의 공격에서 투표 시스템과 개표 시스템이 침투당할 수 있었습니다.  통합선거인명부에 인터넷을 통한 접근이 가능했습니다.  망 분리가 제대로 작동하지 않았고 일부 장비에는 12345라는 비밀번호가 사용됐습니다.  선거관리위원회는 자체적으로 100점을 부여했습니다.  그러나 같은 기준으로 다시 평가했을 때 31.5점을 받았습니다.  국정원은 이것이 기술적 보안점검이지 과거 선거가 조작됐다는 증거는 아니라고 밝혔습니다.  맞습니다. 그렇기 때문에 조사가 필요한 것입니다.  취약점은 얼마나 오랫동안 존재했습니까?  과거 선거에서도 존재했습니까?  누군가 실제로 접근을 시도했습니까?  접속 기록은 보존됐습니까?  독립적인 디지털 포렌식 조사는 이루어졌습니까?  동일한 질문이 6년 동안 반복된다면 한국에 필요한 것은 또 다른 정치적 논쟁이 아닙니다.  필요한 것은 디지털 포렌식입니다.  중국은 한국을 먼 나라로 취급하지 않습니다.  2026년 미국의 한 연구기관이 중국 인민해방군 연계 연구를 검토한 결과, 중국 연구자들이 한국 정치, 한국어, 소셜미디어, 한국인의 여론과 감정 분석, 한국 선거를 연구했다는 내용이 확인됐습니다.  왜 인민해방군 연계 연구자들이 한국의 선거를 연구하고 있습니까?  한국 국가정보원은 중국 기업들이 한국 언론사로 위장한 웹사이트를 운영한 사실을 확인했습니다.  국제 사이버 위협 분석에서도 중국 연계 영향력 네트워크가 한국어 콘텐츠를 이용해 한국 내부의 정치적 갈등을 증폭시키려 했다는 정황이 추적됐습니다.  서로 다른 기관이지만 방향은 같습니다.  중국은 한국의 여론을 관찰하는 데 그치지 않고 한국 정치와 선거 인프라까지 살펴보고 있습니다.  미국이 인도·태평양에서 중국의 팽창을 막으려 한다면, 최전선 동맹국의 선거 시스템을 외부 연구의 대상으로 방치할 수 있겠습니까?
기후 위기, 사이버 공격, 적대국의 위협 등에 따른 대규모 비상사태에 대비하기 위한 조치다.  #비레디 m.edaily.co.kr/News/Read?new…

[영국도 일본도 '3일치 비축' 왜 요즘 각국이 같은 말을 할까]  "물과 식량을 최소 3일치 준비하세요."  영국에 이어 일본에서도 비슷한 안내가 나오면서, 해외 SNS에서는 "각국 정부가 뭔가 알고 있는 것 아니냐"는 반응까지 나옵니다. 일본에서도 "거대 지진의 전조냐"며 불안해하는 글이 퍼졌습니다.  각국의 대비 메시지가 예전보다 눈에 띄게 강해진 건 맞습니다. 하지만 들여다보면 모두가 같은 위험을 예상하고 동시에 움직이는 건 아닙니다.  ▸ 일본, 11월 2일 전 국민에 '긴급요청'  일본에서는 재난 대응을 총괄하는 새 사령탑 '방재청'이 출범하는 11월 2일, 중앙부처와 전국 지방자치단체, 그리고 국민을 대상으로 재난 대비를 강화하라는 '긴급요청'이 나올 예정입니다.  호소노 고시 방재담당상은 공공 지원이 없어도 집에서 버틸 수 있도록 식량과 물, 휴대용 화장실을 최소 3일, 가능하면 1주일치 준비해달라고 했습니다. 가구가 넘어지거나 건물이 무너지는 데 대한 대비도 함께 당부할 계획입니다. 법적 의무가 아니라 국민에게 준비를 요청하는 것입니다.  호소노 장관은 방재청의 가장 큰 임무로 일본 남쪽 바다의 난카이 트로프(남해 해곡) 지진과 수도권 직하 지진 같은 '국난급' 재난 대응을 꼽았습니다. 일본·쿠릴 해구의 거대 지진과 후지산 분화도 전국적인 피해가 우려되는 재난입니다.  다만 '최소 3일, 가능하면 1주일'이라는 기준 자체는 새로운 게 아닙니다. 일본 정부는 동일본대지진 이후인 2013년 무렵부터 같은 기준으로 가정 비축을 권해왔습니다.  달라진 건 새 방재청 출범에 맞춰 장관이 직접 '긴급요청'이라는 강한 말로 다시 강조했다는 점입니다.  ▸ 영국도 며칠 전 '3일 버티기' 캠페인 시작  영국 정부도 지난 22일 새 'Be Ready' 캠페인을 시작했습니다.  정전이나 단수, 인터넷·통신 장애, 홍수와 산불, 심한 폭풍이나 사이버 사고가 났을 때 집에서 3일을 버틸 수 있도록 물과 보존식품, 손전등, 보조배터리, 라디오, 필수 의약품 등을 준비하라는 내용입니다.  한 번 하고 끝나는 안내도 아닙니다. 영국 정부는 앞으로 3년에 걸쳐 국민의 비상 대비 습관을 기르겠다며, 우선 잉글랜드와 웨일스 가정을 위한 체크리스트를 내놨습니다.  영국 정부는 프랑스와 아일랜드, 네덜란드 등 유럽 국가들이 이미 비슷한 대비 지침을 운영하고 있다며 영국도 그 수준에 맞추려는 것이라고 설명했습니다.  ▸ 왜 다들 하필 '3일'일까?  72시간은 갑자기 나온 숫자가 아닙니다.  EU는 지난해 내놓은 대비전략에서 비상사태가 생겼을 때 회원국 국민이 최소 72시간 동안 스스로 생활할 수 있도록 하는 것을 공식 목표로 삼았습니다.  여기서 말하는 비상사태는 전쟁 하나만을 뜻하지 않습니다. 지정학적 갈등과 사이버 공격부터 대규모 정전, 홍수·산불 같은 자연재해와 감염병까지 폭넓게 대비하는 방식입니다.  재난 직후에는 정부와 구조기관이 모든 가정에 동시에 물과 식량을 전할 수 없습니다.  그래서 스스로 버틸 수 있는 사람은 처음 며칠을 버티고, 정부 지원은 노인이나 장애인, 부상자처럼 당장 도움이 필요한 사람에게 먼저 집중하겠다는 것이 72시간 비축의 기본 논리입니다.  일본 장관도 공공 지원 없이 집에서 버틸 수 있어야 한다고 했고, 영국 정부 역시 가정에서 3일을 버티면 응급서비스가 정말 도움이 필요한 사람에게 집중할 수 있다고 설명합니다.  '3일'은 어떤 사건까지 남은 시간이 아니라, 대형 재난이 터졌을 때 국가의 손길이 모두에게 닿기 전까지 각자가 먼저 버텨달라는 시간입니다.  ▸ 그렇다고 분위기가 예전과 똑같은 것도 아니다  일본처럼 오래전부터 있던 지침도 있지만, 영국은 올해 새 3개년 캠페인을 시작했고 EU도 지난해 '72시간 자립'을 유럽 차원의 대비전략에 넣었습니다.  배경도 자연재해만이 아닙니다. EU는 지정학적 긴장과 전쟁, 사이버·하이브리드 위협, 기후변화와 자연재해가 동시에 복잡해지고 있다고 공식적으로 설명하고 있습니다.  각국이 어떤 임박한 사건을 알고 움직인다는 근거는 없습니다.  다만 정부들이 "재난이 닥친 뒤 대응하는 것"에서 "평소 국민까지 미리 준비시키는 것"으로 무게를 옮기고 있는 흐름은 분명해졌습니다.  예전부터 있던 '비상식량 3일치'가 요즘 유난히 자주 눈에 띄는 이유입니다.

Binance, 지난 한 주간 북한 연계 사이버 공격 여러 건 차단... 자산 손실은 없음  Binance는 10월 27일, 보안팀이 지난 한 주 동안 북한과 연계된 여러 건의 사이버 공격을 성공적으로 식별하고 차단했으며, 회사 시스템 피해나 자산 손실은 없었다고 밝힘.   Binance는 북한 연계 해킹 그룹이 "Contagious Interview" 캠페인 하에 허위 채용 면접, 코딩 테스트, 소프트웨어 설치 요청 등을 이용해 대상자가 악성 프로그램을 실행하도록 유도하는 사회 공학적 공격을 지속하고 있다고 언급함.   해당 거래소는 사용자들에게 승인되지 않은 소프트웨어를 설치하거나 신뢰할 수 없는 소스의 코드를 실행하지 말라고 권고하며, 보안 모니터링, 위협 탐지 및 내부 보안 통제를 지속적으로 강화할 것이라고 덧붙임.

[ AI가 스스로 사이버보안 붐을 만든다... "AI 능력이 커질수록 보안 수요도 커진다", 2027년 보안 예산 7% 증가 ]  BofA는 PHP2Shell 취약점을 또 하나의 경고음으로 본다.   AI가 기계 속도로 보안 결함을 찾아내고 악용하는 단계에 들어서면서 탐지와 취약점 관리, 위협 사냥, AI 기반 보안 운영이 모두 더 중요해졌다.   AI 능력이 강해질수록 보안 수요는 커진다는 논리.   BofA CIO 설문에서 2027년 사이버 예산은 7% 늘어 전체 소프트웨어 지출 증가율을 앞서고, CIO 절반은 7% 이상 증가를 예상한다.   BofA는 크라우드스트라이크, 체크포인트, 세일포인트, 지스케일러 목표주가를 올렸다. 수요가 재량적 지출이 아니라 구조적 지출로 바뀌고 있다는 판단이다.  구조적 강세론의 다른 축은 아직 시장이 사후 대응 단계라는 점..   세계경제포럼 보고서에 따르면 조직의 절반 이상이 사고가 터진 뒤에야 보안에 투자하고, 투자수익을 근거로 투자하는 곳은 8%뿐이다.   보안이 IT 비용에서 전략 투자로 바뀌는 과정이 길게 남아 있다는 뜻이다. 사이버 리스크는 거시 리스크가 되고 있다.   심각한 사고 한 번이 그해 GDP의 0.2%에서 2%를 날릴 수 있는데, 보안을 경제 안정 장치로 보는 조직은 9%에 불과하다.  지출 사이클은 둔화 기미가 없다.   SG 추정으로 2026년 글로벌 정보보안 지출은 약 2,400억 달러로 연 12.5%에서 13.3% 성장해 5년 연속 두 자릿수 확장이다.   IT 예산에서 보안 비중은 2020년 8.6%에서 13%로 올랐다. AI 증폭 보안 시장은 2025년 490억 달러에서 2029년 1,600억 달러로 3배 넘게 커질 전망이다.  AI는 공격의 경제학을 바꿨다.   SG에 따르면 악성코드의 76%가 AI 기반으로 스스로 형태를 바꾸고, 피싱과 자격증명 탈취, 취약점 악용이 자동화되고 있다.  방어자도 자동화로 맞설 수밖에 없고 가트너는 2026년 AI 보안 지출이 두 배 가까이 늘 것으로 본다.   다만 구조는 계속 공격자에게 유리하다.   공격자는 구매 절차와 규정 심사가 없고, 방어자는 모든 자산을 지켜야 하는데 공격자는 뚫린 길 하나면 되며, 가짜 콘텐츠를 만드는 건 싸고 진위를 검증하는 건 비싸다.   AI 능력이 빨리 발전할수록 AI 보안 솔루션의 구조적 수요는 더 강해진다.
PHP 보안취약점 발견, Node.js 취약점 발견... 매일 새로운 취약점이 발견된다.   AI로 인해 사이버 위협 주기가 극단적으로 짧아진 2026년의 현실이다. IT 운영팀은 패치에 대한 대응 속도를 어떻게 따라잡을지가 핵심 과제가 될 듯.

앤스로픽이 예측한 2030년, AI가 불러올 충격적인 미래 🤖  관련 영상은 댓글에   1. 2030년 AI 전망은 극단적으로 엇갈린다  - 한쪽에서는 현재의 AI 열기가 부풀려진 과장이라고 본다  - 반대편에서는 인류가 이미 기술적 특이점에 들어섰다고 주장한다  2. 과거의 파격적인 예측을 현실로 만든 앤스로픽  - 앤스로픽은 강력한 AI의 등장 시기를 다른 주요 개발사보다 이르게 예상했다  - 코딩과 사이버 보안 분야에서는 AI의 역할이 이미 크게 확대됐다  - 여러 AI 에이전트가 동시에 연구·개발하는 구상도 작동 중이다  3. 현재 AI에는 신중하지만 2030년 전망은 크게 낙관한다  - 현재 AI 능력에 대한 평가는 직원과 일반인이 비슷하거나 직원 쪽이 더 낮다  - 2030년의 능력 전망에서는 두 집단의 응답이 크게 벌어진다  - AI 사용 경험이 많을수록 AI의 미래 능력을 크게 예상하는 경향이 나타난다  4. 업무 자동화는 해고보다 신입 채용 축소로 먼저 나타난다  - 직원들은 자신의 업무 중 큰 부분이 AI로 대체될 것으로 본다  - 당장 인원이 줄기보다 신규 기술직 채용에서 신입의 몫이 줄었다  5. 실업률은 금융위기 수준을 넘을 수 있지만 경제성장률은 급등할 수 있다  - AI 업무 대체가 커질수록 실업률 전망도 높아진다  - 높은 실업률 전망과 함께 경제성장률도 크게 오른다  - 일자리는 줄고 경제는 팽창하는 낯선 조합이 제시된다  6. 성장의 이익과 일자리 상실의 고통은 고르게 나뉘지 않는다  - 2030년 전망의 핵심은 성장과 실업의 동시 발생이다  - 노동소득 몫은 줄고 일자리를 잃은 사람의 재취업은 어려워질 수 있다  - 재교육과 소득 지원 등 분배 장치를 경제 정책의 중심에 둬야 한다  - 개인과 사회가 함께 변화에 대비해야 한다

북한 IP 대역에서 국내 금융권을 겨냥한 스캔성 접근이 440만 건 넘게 탐지됐음.  10월 21일 새벽 3시부터 몰렸고, 공문 시점까지 4,404,101건이었다 함.  금감원은 보안관제시스템 '퍼스트'로 금융사에 공문을 보내 보안·내부통제·실시간 모니터링 점검을 당부했음.  스캔성 접근은 열린 포트나 취약점을 찾는 '문 두드리기'임.  같은 날 대신증권 고객 3만8490명 정보 유출, 빗썸·미래에셋운용 피해까지 터졌음.   400만 번 두드리면 언젠가 열린다는 걸 아는 듯함. 설마 이거도 서버 비밀번호 12345인가요?

Trojanized LiteLLM 1.107.0 pushed to PyPI and Docker on Oct 21 hooks Python's startup routine to steal credentials before any app code runs. Supply chain attack traced to a months-old unrotated key that handed attackers full CI/CD control.  Key findings:  - The attack chain began May 27 when an opencode.json file containing a master key was committed to a public repo, overwritten but never rotated. By October 10 the attacker used that key to query the Agent Platform API, retrieved a GitHub CLI OAuth token for a BerriAI org owner (bypassing 2FA), then on October 21 stood up a typosquatted repo named Berri-AI/litellm and hijacked the official release pipeline. A second compromised maintainer account was used to approve the production deployment. The attacker maintained access for 11 days before deploying the payload.  - The malicious files cook.pth, cook[.]py, and sitecustomize[.]py land in the root site-packages directory, not the litellm/ package folder. cook.pth fires a single-line "import cook" at interpreter startup, cook[.]py Base64/zlib-decodes an embedded payload (internally labeled PRIVCOLLECT) and runs it in a daemon thread, and sitecustomize[.]py runs a polling loop that fetches a live C2 address from raw.githubusercontent[.]com/letters9813/pythonclient-test/main/domain[.]txt then compiles and executes whatever code the /codepy endpoint returns, all in memory with no signature check. TTPs: T1195.001, T1574, T1059.006, T1102.001.  - The credential harvester targets AI coding assistant configs, IDE auth files, source control and package manager credentials, .env files, cloud CLI credential caches, container service-account files, procfs process environments on Linux, browser credential stores and history (Chromium and Firefox, T1555.003), SSH and GPG key material, CI/CD and Vault configs, and LiteLLM proxy database tables via an ORM child process (500-row limit per table). Collected data is AES-256-CBC encrypted with a fresh 32-byte key per run, the session key is wrapped with a hardcoded 4096-bit RSA public key, then exfiltrated via HTTP POST to hxxp://www.litellm[.]dev/healthcheck with header X-Token: XWiA8gZNa7NcX2XRoAEb and the payload hash in X-SHA256 (T1041, T1560.002). A sentinel file at /tmp/.pc_once_72129118c59f5636c0bb marks successful exfiltration; /tmp/remote_code_loader.lock prevents duplicate RAT instances.  - Confirmed SHA-256 hashes for the poisoned wheels: macOS x86-64 sha256:7598727f209d717041db37f7dca271d3a7d328a279890e0e1d55375729aeb86d, macOS ARM64 sha256:0aaf7ba346d41ef2f40390436738b001180d5a1c03aa093f121078a9969d9a1a, Linux manylinux x86-64 sha256:462d0c9f67ca522d9e0e4acd245e90b36ce0d5353604a66bb7c43a1ec4a6fcf7, Linux manylinux ARM64 sha256:668169d35b87bf51324080390b1b1c5ab12bd335cfe5f1a99e3689abd5e02ae6, Linux musllinux x86-64 sha256:1bbce8caa94f01c0aaa0b7ddae51553a8a32e1ce53d96d44fe583272aff7ad00, Linux musllinux ARM64 sha256:c2e32d0ce2548aa662c18bf5001911a79fe5b30cf8357132275add02fdcde054, Windows x86-64 sha256:12d4ccc5c6f8d35cf4f2cf233b7f3e418e863e657d81ff5f5fc9e210005b9484. Docker image index sha256:1bbcb1443bc962e45f5aad53fe3d2c30600e0379715fb6c664cdd3ac126c339e.  Practitioner takeaway: Do not invoke Python or pip inside a suspect environment to check for the package; that alone triggers the payload. Hunt site-packages for cook.pth, cook[.]py, and sitecustomize[.]py, and check /tmp for .pc_once_72129118c59f5636c0bb and remote_code_loader.lock. Watch egress for POST traffic to litellm[.]dev and DNS queries resolving through raw.githubusercontent[.]com to the letters9813 path. Remediation requires full environment rebuild, not uninstall. Treat every secret accessible to the affected process as compromised and rotate immediately. IOCs, hashes, and ATT&CK mappings are in the ThreatMon report.  #DFIR_Radar

The Doorway botnet has systematically compromised routers, cameras, and enterprise servers globally, with 11,363 device joins recorded in a single hour and 41 GB of operational data left exposed by the operators themselves.  Key findings:  - CloudSEK's investigation began with 41 GB of exposed operational data left accessible by the Doorway operators, revealing the inner workings of the campaign at an unusual level of detail. The data contained 59 exploit modules targeting IoT devices, network gear, and enterprise servers, alongside automated credential stuffing logic designed to move through device populations at scale.  - The attack chain combines known vulnerability exploitation with brute-force credential attacks. Devices compromised include consumer and enterprise routers, surveillance cameras, and servers, all folded into proxy infrastructure rather than used for traditional DDoS or spam purposes. The botnet's primary value appears to be as a commercial proxy network, routing third-party traffic through victim devices.  - The 11,363 device joins in a single hour is the sharpest indicator of the campaign's operational tempo. At that rate, device turnover and fresh compromise happen continuously, meaning the active device count understates total victim exposure across the campaign's lifetime.  - The 59 exploit modules represent a broad targeting surface. Rather than focusing on a single vendor or CVE, the Doorway operation maintains a module library that can be aimed at whichever device population presents the weakest resistance, a characteristic of mature, commercially motivated botnet operations rather than a targeted threat actor.  Practitioners responding to suspected proxy abuse or unexplained outbound traffic on IoT or network devices should pull authentication logs for rapid sequential failed logins followed by a success, check for new or modified scheduled tasks, cron jobs, and startup scripts, and look for outbound connections to unfamiliar IPs on non-standard ports that persist across reboots. The CloudSEK report contains the IOC details from the exposed operational data.  #DFIR_Radar

Backups are not an incident-response strategy unless recovery has been tested.  Ransomware and account compromise can affect more than endpoints. Microsoft 365 environments hold mail, documents, identity relationships, and business workflows that teams may assume can always be recovered.  The useful metric is not “we have backups.” It is how quickly the organization can restore critical operations without restoring the attacker’s foothold with them.  In practical terms, it is a good time to: • Test restoration of critical mail and collaboration data. • Review backup administrative roles and access paths. • Validate separation between production identities and backup administration. • Include Microsoft 365 recovery dependencies in ransomware tabletop exercises.  #Ransomware #IncidentResponse #CyberResilience #CloudSecurity guardiandigital.com/resource…

GPU Infrastructure Is Becoming a Platform Engineering Challenge, Not Just a Hardware Investment  Introduction  The rapid growth of artificial intelligence has made advanced GPUs a central component of digital infrastructure. Yet purchasing accelerators is only the beginning of building a useful compute service.  A production-ready GPU platform must coordinate hardware, power delivery, cooling, storage, networking, security, scheduling, monitoring, and software deployment. It must also provide a consistent experience for the people and organizations using the infrastructure.  This changes the central question from “Which GPU should we buy?” to “What complete platform can we operate reliably and economically?”  1. From Individual Accelerators to Integrated Platforms  A GPU can perform complex calculations, but commercial workloads depend on a broader environment.  The system requires compatible host processors, sufficient system memory, storage capable of supporting the workload, appropriate networking, and software that can allocate resources correctly.  For multi-GPU systems, these dependencies become more significant. Power distribution, thermal design, topology, and communication paths must be engineered together.  A mismatch in one component can constrain the entire platform.  2. Power and Cooling Are Performance Variables  Advanced accelerators can impose substantial power and thermal demands. When deployed at scale, these demands affect electrical infrastructure, rack design, facility cooling, and operating costs.  Cooling is not merely a facility expense. It influences the environment in which GPUs maintain sustained operation.  Poor thermal management can cause performance throttling, instability, or premature component degradation. Inadequate power planning can limit expansion or create reliability risks.  Operators should therefore evaluate accelerator specifications together with actual system power, cooling requirements, rack density, and facility constraints.  Liquid cooling can be valuable for high-density deployments, but it is not automatically necessary or economical for every workload. The correct approach depends on the specific hardware and facility design.  3. Scheduling Determines How Much Capacity Becomes Revenue  A GPU platform needs an effective way to allocate resources among competing workloads.  Different customers may require different GPU memory capacities, performance levels, security boundaries, software environments, and service durations.  A scheduling system must consider these requirements while minimizing idle time and avoiding resource conflicts.  For example, a large training workload may need several GPUs working together, while an inference service may benefit from smaller allocations distributed across many requests.  The platform must match each workload to suitable resources rather than treating every GPU hour as equally valuable.  4. Isolation and Security Are Essential for Shared Compute  When multiple customers share infrastructure, security becomes part of the service itself.  Operators need to define access controls, workload isolation, image management, secrets handling, logging, patching, and incident-response procedures.  Depending on the threat model, additional measures may be necessary to protect sensitive workloads or data in use.  Customers should understand what the provider guarantees, what remains their responsibility, and how failures or security incidents are handled.  A platform that offers raw compute without clear operational boundaries may struggle to earn the trust of serious enterprise users.
